target_customer: Developers running multiple AI coding agents in parallel git worktrees on one machine
problem: Parallel agents on git worktrees collide on ports, databases and per-branch setup. Coasts gives each worktree its own containerized runtime.
business_model: Free open source (MIT) CLI; monetization not described

founders.name: Jamie Sunderland
prior_employers: Y Combinator (product engineer, built investor CRM)
previous_startups: Cheqout (YC W21, QR restaurant ordering, 250+ restaurants)

founders.name: Dan Hyman
founders.background_notes: From the YC page JSX Tool section.

exit.reason: YC lists Inactive, but the site, GitHub project and blog appear live with 2026 dates; no shutdown or acquisition found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Docker-in-Docker host isolation with per-worktree ports and shared services is substantial systems work for two people; Hacker News coverage describes about 200MB overhead per host and macOS-first support.

defensibility.rationale: MIT licensed open source with no network or data moat, and parallel-agent worktree tools were multiplying.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No documented acquisition or copy as of the sources.

market_need_then: Developers reported port clashes when running parallel agents across worktrees; the Show HN post of 2026-03-30 and articles on worktrees for AI agents show demand, though a skeptical HN commenter called the workflow overcomplicated.

branding.name_origin: Each instance is called a Coast, defined by the project blog as a containerized host.
branding.domain_note: coasts.dev; legal entity shown as Stanton Street Inc.
branding.community_and_virality: Show HN post on 2026-03-30 with roughly 400 GitHub stars at crawl time (snapshots differ); Discord and blog linked on the site.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear metaphor fits the product and the HN launch gave some visibility, but the term Coast collides with many unrelated companies in search.

outcome_analysis: Coasts joined YC in Fall 2025 from a second-time founder and a cloud engineer, shipped a free open source tool and got a modest Show HN launch in March 2026. YC lists it as Inactive yet its site and repository show 2026 activity, so the status may reflect a YC data flag rather than a shutdown, and no cause or funding information is public.
notes: No funding source found: searches returned only unrelated companies named Coast; the YC standard deal is not recorded because no source states an amount. Competitors left empty: worktree tooling found (Superset, ChatML, wt) has undated or post-batch Show HN items. The YC page links a launch post for sibling JSX Tool, not Coasts. Education not found. Inactive status conflicts with a live site, cause not public.
